items.title: Alberta personal and family responsibility leave
items.body: Eligible employees in Alberta can take up to 5 days of unpaid, job-protected leave each calendar year to meet family responsibilities for a family member. You give your employer notice as soon as is reasonable before taking the leave.
quotes: Employees are eligible for personal and family responsibility leave if they have been employed at least 90 days with the same employer.
Employees with less than 90 days of employment may still be granted leave.
An employee must give an employer notice as soon as is reasonable before taking a leave.
The legislation entitles eligible employees to a period of leave without pay, at the end of which they must be reinstated in their same, or an equivalent, job.
A medical certificate or other documentation is not required by legislation
items.notes: unpaid unless an employment contract or collective agreement says otherwise

items.title: EI caregiving benefits
items.body: EI caregiving benefits may apply if a medical doctor or nurse practitioner certifies that the person is critically ill or injured, or needs end-of-life care. Other eligibility requirements apply; this is not an eligibility decision.
quotes: Their condition must be certified by a medical doctor or nurse practitioner.
A critically ill or injured person is someone whose baseline state of health has changed significantly because of illness or injury.
End-of-life care is defined as providing care or support to a person who has a serious medical condition with a significant risk of death within 26 weeks (6 months).
items.notes: family caregiver benefit for adults up to 15 weeks, for children up to 35 weeks, compassionate care benefits up to 26 weeks
